form.label: Findings
form.description: Every vulnerability the current feed can attribute to installed software.

div.span: Select rows to accept a risk. Every selected row must share one CVE - one justification cannot honestly cover several different vulnerabilities.

panel.title: Findings, ranked by exploitation likelihood (EPSS) rather than CVSS

search.query: | `riskability_open_findings_all_for($host_tok|s$, $package_tok|s$, $cve_tok|s$, $confidence_tok|s$)` | search $scope_tok$ | eval installed_version = last_version | eval epss_pct = if(isnotnull(epss), round(epss*100, 2), null()) | eval kev = if(kev_added!="", "yes", "") | eval accepted_label = if(accepted=="1", "accepted", "") | table cve_id, package, installed_version, fixed_version, hostname, scope_id, ecosystem, match_authority, confidence, epss_pct, kev, accepted_label, title, finding_key | rename cve_id AS "CVE", package AS "Package", installed_version AS "Installed", fixed_version AS "Fixed in", hostname AS "Host", scope_id AS "Root", ecosystem AS "Type", match_authority AS "Authority", confidence AS "Confidence", epss_pct AS "EPSS %", kev AS "KEV", accepted_label AS "Accepted", title AS "Summary", finding_key AS "Key" | sort 50000 - "EPSS %"

viz.option: No findings matched. With the Confidence filter on "High only" this can mean the evidence was never strong enough to assert one, not that the fleet is clean - switch it to All to see what was found and why it was downgraded.

div.b: The column filters narrow what is shown, not what was searched.
div.span: Typing in a column header filters the rows already loaded into the page. It does not re-run the search, so it cannot reach findings the search did not return, and it does not change the panels on any other dashboard. For anything you intend to act on, narrow it with the Confidence, Root and Host inputs above, which filter in the search itself. "Download shown rows" likewise exports what is currently displayed and filtered, not the whole result set.

html.p: Confidence is about the strength of the evidence, not the severity of the vulnerability.

ul.li: high - a distro or ecosystem advisory names this package and release, and both versions parsed cleanly under that ecosystem's rules.

informational - an upstream version range covers a distribution package. Ubuntu and Red Hat backport fixes without changing the upstream version, so openssl 3.0.13-0ubuntu3.4 may well already be patched against a CVE that upstream fixed in 3.0.14. Shown so it is not hidden; not asserted, because it is not known.
low - the comparison could not be made properly: no comparator for the ecosystem, an unparseable version such as UNKNOWN, or an identity inferred from a binary rather than a package record.
